title: Synchronized motion of interface residues for evaluating protein-RNA complex binding affinity: Application to aptamer-mediated inhibition of TDP-43 aggregates.
authors: Panei, Francesco Paolo; Di Rienzo, Lorenzo; Zacco, Elsa; Armaos, Alexandros; Tartaglia, Gian Gaetano; Ruocco, Giancarlo; Milanetti, Edoardo
journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
one_liner_zh: 该文通过对接、聚类和分子动力学模拟，基于界面残基同步运动评估蛋白-RNA适配体结合亲和力，虽为蛋白-RNA互作体系，但方法可迁移至TF-DNA互作建模，故评6分。
abstract: Investigating the binding between proteins and aptamers, such as peptides or RNA molecules, is of crucial importance both for understanding the molecular mechanisms that regulate cellular activities and for therapeutic applications in several pathologies. Here, a new computational procedure, employing mainly docking, clustering analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations, was designed to estimate the binding affinities between a protein and some RNA aptamers, through the investigation of the dynamical behavior of the predicted molecular complex. Using the state-of-the-art software catRAPID, we computationally designed a set of RNA aptamers interacting with the TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43), a protein associated with several neurodegenerative diseases, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). We thus devised a computational protocol to predict the RNA-protein molecular complex, so that the structural and dynamical behavior of such a complex can be investigated through extensive molecular dynamics simulation. We hypothesized that the coordinated and synchronized motion of the protein-binding residues, when in contact with RNA molecule, is a critical requisite in order to have a stable binding. Indeed, we calculated the motion covariance exhibited by the interface residues during molecular dynamics simulation: we tested the results against experimental measurements of binding affinity (in this case, the dissociation constant) for six RNA molecules, resulting in a linear correlation of about 0.9. Our findings suggest that the synchronized movement of interface residues plays a pivotal role in ensuring the stability within RNA-protein complexes, moreover providing insights into the contribution of each interface residue. This promising pipeline could thus contribute to the design of RNA aptamers interacting with proteins.
abstract_zh: 研究蛋白质与适配体（如肽或RNA分子）之间的结合，对于理解调控细胞活动的分子机制以及多种病理学中的治疗应用至关重要。在此，我们设计了一种新的计算流程，主要采用对接、聚类分析和分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟，通过预测的分子复合物的动力学行为来估算蛋白质与某些RNA适配体之间的结合亲和力。利用最先进的软件catRAPID，我们计算设计了一组与TAR DNA结合蛋白43 (TDP-43) 相互作用的RNA适配体，该蛋白与多种神经退行性疾病相关，包括肌萎缩侧索硬化症 (ALS)。因此，我们设计了一个计算协议来预测RNA-蛋白质分子复合物，从而可以通过广泛的分子动力学模拟研究此类复合物的结构和动力学行为。我们假设，蛋白质结合残基在与RNA分子接触时的协调同步运动，是实现稳定结合的关键必要条件。确实，我们计算了分子动力学模拟过程中界面残基表现出的运动协方差：我们将结果与六个RNA分子的实验结合亲和力（此处为解离常数）测量值进行了测试，得出约0.9的线性相关性。我们的发现表明，界面残基的同步运动在确保RNA-蛋白质复合物稳定性中起着关键作用，同时为每个界面残基的贡献提供了见解。这一有前景的流程因此可能有助于设计与蛋白质相互作用的RNA适配体。
